articleTitle: Design and Development of a Modular Mission Control Board for Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of open-source (OS) software into embedded systems has garnered great attention, especially in the field of autonomy. There is a growing demand for hardware that is not only versatile but also high-performing and low-cost in the realm of autonomous systems (ASs). Traditional closed systems can be restrictive for developers and researchers due to their limited customization options and high costs. OS software platforms provide a solution to this problem, allowing users to adapt the software to their needs and benefit from a wide community support. This study focuses on the hardware design and development of a mission control board that can run OS software such as ArduPilot and PX4. The main goal is to provide a flexible and cost-effective hardware platform for autonomous vehicle enthusiasts, researchers, and developers. This hardware platform will respond to the increasing demand for flexible and high-performance ASs. Thanks to its modular design, users can customize the board for specific applications such as mapping, delivery, and autonomous navigation. It offers the opportunity to benefit from extensive documentation, community support, and many features, especially thanks to its compatibility with OS ecosystems. The board development and testing stages were primarily carried out on aircraft. However, the ultimate goal is to expand the card to various ASs, such as unmanned ground vehicles and marine vessels, and increase its applicability in these areas. Preliminary tests demonstrate the effectiveness of the card effectiveness, stability, and ease of use in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning-Based Image Preprocessing and Classification for Kidney Disease Detection in CT Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Kidney diseases are serious medical conditions that have life-threatening consequences. Because of their impact on patient health, they are an important area of medical research. Medical imaging coupled with deep learning methods and models have proven effective in diagnosing kidney diseases. In this study, we investigated the accuracy of image-processing methods, namely edge detection and contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE), for the detection of normal kidneys, kidney cysts, kidney tumors, and kidney stones. The results suggest that CLAHE is the more suitable image-processing method when the ResNet50 deep learning architecture is used to detect and diagnose kidney diseases, with an accuracy of 92%, compared with 84% for edge detection.

articleTitle: Atom Search Optimizer-driven Lead Compensator Design for Unstable Ball and Beam System
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: This study proposes a novel framework for stabilizing the inherently unstable ball and beam system by combining a classical lead compensator with the atom search optimizer (ASO). The ball and beam setup, widely recognized as a benchmark for evaluating control strategies, poses significant challenges due to its open-loop instability and nonlinear dynamics. To address these issues, we formulate the design of a lead compensator in terms of an integral of absolute error (IAE) cost function, with constraints that ensure a genuine phase-lead characteristic. ASO automatically tunes the compensator parameters by iteratively minimizing the IAE criterion while respecting the required pole–zero placement. Simulation results compare the ASO-based controller against genetic algorithm, sine-cosine algorithm, and a root locus–based method. The ASO-driven design consistently achieves faster settling, lower overshoot, and reduced IAE under both linearized and nonlinear plant representations. Overall, the proposed scheme demonstrates not only robust tracking performance but also adaptability to the system’s nonlinearities, confirming the effectiveness of metaheuristic optimization for real-world control applications.

articleTitle: Safety Performance Assessment by Harnessing IoT and AI in Construction Sites: Leveraging Digital Tools for Safer Construction Practices
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: At present, the safety performance evaluation technology of soil and aluminum in the construction site has the problems of poor design effect and poor comfort. Therefore, this paper studies the digital safety in the safety performance evaluation technology of soil and aluminum in the building site. Put forward the safety performance evaluation technology optimization method of the building site soil and aluminum based on the digital security algorithm. Firstly, extract the building site scene information through the digital security framework, and realize the digital security method and the fusion of digital security nodes. Then, the digital security algorithm is used to optimize the digital safety design of the safety performance evaluation technology of soil and aluminum, and to optimize the safety performance evaluation technology of soil and aluminum. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the construction of soil and aluminum safety performance evaluation technology, improve the construction of soil and aluminum safety performance evaluation technology of farmers building soil and aluminum safety performance assessment environment, optimize the construction of soil and aluminum safety performance evaluation technology experience.

articleTitle: Research on Consumer Privacy Concerns and Willingness to use Intelligent Systems from the Perspective of Informatics
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: At present, intelligent technology has been widely used, and consumers' concern about privacy has become one of the important factors affecting the sales of intelligent systems. In order to understand the impact of privacy concerns on consumers' willingness to use smart systems, and to explore the moderating role of trust and transparency, this paper will conduct an in-depth analysis from the perspective of informatics. This paper uses questionnaire design to collect core indicator data, such as privacy concerns and trust, transparency, and willingness to use. During the research process, a structured questionnaire is designed first, data is collected at the same time, and the necessary data cleaning and pre-processing are carried out to make the data accurate and complete. Then, through descriptive analysis, the basic characteristics of the sample were understood, and confirmatory factor analysis was carried out to verify the structural validity of the table, and finally, the structural equation model was used to analyze the complex relationship between the variables, and at the same time, the fit of the model was evaluated. In addition, this paper conducts a survey through an actual questionnaire that collects data from 500-1000 consumers of intelligent systems. Through the analysis, it can be seen that the root mean square error value of the model reaches 0.05, which indicates that the fit degree of the model is good, which indicates that informatics has unique advantages in processing multi-dimensional data and complex system analysis, and can provide a scientific basis for the design and promotion of intelligent systems.

articleTitle: Impact of Silent Regions on Spoofed Speech Detection: A Deep Learning Based Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Silent regions in speech signals can significantly impact the training performance of spoofing detection models. The literature suggests that models primarily rely on silent regions to distinguish between genuine and spoofed speech, as genuine speech typically contains more silence segments. This study analyzes the effect of silent regions on the training and generalization capability of developed models by evaluating test results from various deep learning models and presenting the findings comparatively. A balanced subset was created from the ASVSpoof 2019 LA dataset, ensuring an equal number of genuine and spoofed speech samples. The speech files in this subset were processed using a Voice Activity Detection (VAD) algorithm to remove silent regions. For the experimental study, Spoofing Detection (SD) models were trained and evaluated using baseline models (RawNet2 and LFCC-LCNN) developed for the ASVSpoof 2021 LA dataset, along with Wav2Vec2-ResNet18 models. The results demonstrated a significant degradation in model performance when silent regions were removed from the dataset: LFCC-LCNN exhibited a 15.1% decrease in performance, RawNet2 showed a 69.8% decline, Wav2Vec2-ResNet18 experienced a 30.1% drop. These findings confirm that silent regions play a critical role in the performance of spoofing detection models. The study further reveals that removing silence information significantly reduces the models’ ability to distinguish between genuine and spoofed speech.

articleTitle: AI-Assisted Cross-Cultural Communication Barrier Identification and Solution Research
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Cross-cultural communication barriers identification belongs to assist is the sustainable development of artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence auxiliary cross-cultural communication obstacle identification, to a certain extent to protect the cross-cultural communication obstacle identification environment, reduce communication barriers, therefore, the artificial intelligence auxiliary cross-cultural communication obstacle recognition and the solution of in-depth analysis. First, gray correlation is used to analyze the characteristic indicators of cross-cultural communication obstacle identification and solution assisted by artificial intelligence, so as to build an index system of cross-cultural communication obstacle identification and solution measurement. Then use artificial intelligence to build cross-cultural communication barriers identification and solution control of explanatory variables and control variables, through the principal component analysis of cross-cultural communication barriers identification and solution control of variation factor, the elastic modulus and regression discriminant method, complete artificial intelligence auxiliary cross-cultural communication obstacle identification and the impact of solution analysis. The simulation experiment results show that the algorithm can effectively reduce the operation efficiency of cross-cultural communication obstacle identification, ensure the quality of AI assistance, and protect the environment of cross-cultural communication obstacle identification.

articleTitle: The performance of modified SEPIC converter for dynamic conditions with PI controller
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: DC-DC converters, the input voltage level is transferred to the load at the desired value with appropriate control methods. In recent years, switched-operated DC-DC converters, such as the modified SEPIC converter, have been widely used. These converters improve system performance by reducing power loss and significantly improving energy efficiency. In this study, the performance of the modified SEPIC converter was evaluated under five different scenarios (basic scenario, output voltage increase, load change, input voltage decreases under constant load condition, and load change with simultaneous input voltage decreases). By presenting the dynamic model of the converter and state-space equations, the behavior of the system under the proportional-integral (PI) controller is examined. The modified SEPIC converter was designed in the MATLAB/SIMULINK 2021b environment, simulated and the results were analyzed. The simulation results revealed that the system reacts to the transient regime state in as little as 0.03 seconds, providing 99.99% efficiency with low voltage and current oscillations.

articleTitle: Transformative Methods to Fire Credit Rating: Integrating Data Mining Methods and XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Under the background of fire credit rating XGBoost, to improve the success rate of integrated data mining method optimization, the optimization of integrated data mining method of fire credit rating is studied, but when the traditional method is used for the optimization evaluation of integrated data mining method, there is the problem of poor evaluation accuracy. To this end, an integrated data mining method based on fire credit rating is proposed. Firstly, the fuzzy evaluation theory is adopted to integrate the set of evaluation factors optimized by the data mining method to calculate the weight of each factor and obtain the ratio of the weight of each factor. Then, the integrated data mining method is used to optimize the integrated data mining method, combined with the integrated data mining method, and the evaluation value of the success rate, and complete the optimization of the integrated data mining method under the background of fire credit rating XGBoost. According to the simulation experiment results, the proposed method can effectively improve the effectiveness and reliability of the integrated data mining method.

articleTitle: Research on The Application of Deep Learning-Based Emotion Recognition Technology in Psychological Counseling
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In the emotional information fluctuations and sudden emotional load impact simulation, output learning and outbreak condition, deep learning emotion recognition technology psychological counseling lag problems, may lead to the use of deep learning of emotion recognition technology trigger psychological counseling exploration and design protection, lead to psychological counseling exploration design control effect is poor. Therefore, for the unstable output of emotion information under deep learning conditions, the optimized design method of emotion recognition technology based on deep learning is adopted. Firstly, the paper introduces the analysis model of deep learning system, describes the basic system of emotion recognition technology of deep learning, and analyzes the dynamic modeling process of emotion recognition technology.

articleTitle: Elliptical Antenna Array Synthesis using Puma Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The amplitudes of elliptical antenna arrays with 8, 12, and 20 elements are optimized using the Puma Optimization Algorithm (POA) to suppress the maximum sidelobe level (MSL) and reduce the half-power beamwidth (HPBW). Elliptical antenna arrays are preferred in broadband communication and radar applications due to their high gain and low MSL requirements. POA stands out as an effective method for solving complex optimization problems due to its strong search capability and fast solution time. In this study, simulations are conducted for elliptical antenna arrays with 8, 12, and 20 elements, achieving reduced sidelobe levels and improved main beamwidth. The results demonstrate the successful performance of POA on elliptical antenna arrays. This study highlights the potential of POA for future design applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Remote Sensing for Intelligent Damage Detection in Industrial Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Pipeline systems are vital components of modern industrial infrastructure, ensuring the safe and efficient transportation of fluids such as oil, gas, and chemicals. However, these systems are prone to damage from mechanical stress, corrosion, temperature fluctuations, and environmental factors. Among these, cracks represent the most common form of damage and, if left undetected, can lead to severe environmental hazards, operational downtime, and significant economic losses. Traditional inspection methods, while effective, are often time-consuming, costly, and pose risks to human safety. To address these challenges, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with advanced remote sensing technologies have emerged as promising alternatives for pipeline monitoring. UAVs offer enhanced safety, cost-effectiveness, and efficiency, enabling the rapid detection and assessment of pipeline damage. This study focuses on comparing two prominent object detection algorithms, SSD and YOLOv7, for pipeline damage detection. Both algorithms were tested under varying environmental conditions and pipeline structures to evaluate their accuracy, speed, and reliability. The results demonstrated that SSD achieved a precision of 0.719, a recall of 0.656, and an F1 score of 0.686. In contrast, YOLOv7 outperformed SSD in recall (0.677) and F1 score (0.690), highlighting its superior ability to detect defects. While the speed and simplicity of SSD make it well-suited for real-time applications, YOLOv7’s balanced performance and higher recall make it the preferred choice for scenarios where missing defects is unacceptable. These findings underscore the potential of integrating UAVs with advanced detection algorithms for more effective and reliable pipeline monitoring.

articleTitle: Open-Circuit Fault Detection in T-Type MLI Using XGBoost: A Machine Learning-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Prediction of open circuit (OC) faults in a T-Type multilevel inverter (MLI) with high accuracy using machine learning (ML) models is a critical issue for the reliability of power electronic systems. In this study, OC faults that may occur in any of the nine switches in the inverter circuit are detected and classified using a data-driven approach. K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and XGBoost algorithms are applied for machine learning based fault detection and their performances are compared. The data set for fault detection is obtained from randomly generated OC faults in the T-Type MLI circuit modeled in MATLAB/Simulink environment. For each fault class, 255 signal samples are obtained for two cycles (4 ms) at a sampling frequency of 5 kHz and used as input data to the ML models. The XGBoost model shows the best performance with an accuracy of 98.37%. This shows that it provides fast and reliable fault detection in large data sets. The confusion matrix, accuracy and loss plots are used to analyze the performance of the model and the study demonstrates the applicability of ML-based fault detection in inverter systems.

articleTitle: Classification of Eastern Black Sea Tea Using E-Nose: A Deep Learning-Based CNN Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The Black Sea tea is of significant cultural and economic importance, with its distinct characteristics influenced by factors like soil, climate, and cultivation practices, but its classification often faces challenges due to taster variability and sensory subjectivity. This paper presents a classification approach for different tea types from the Black Sea Region using an electronic nose (e-nose) system. Sensor data obtained from eight Metal Oxide Semiconductor (MOS) sensors were analyzed and classified using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. The study explores the performance of raw sensor data and data transformed through Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). The results indicate that the CNN model achieves high classification accuracy, with the highest accuracy reaching 90.64% using the sensor combination of 2, 4, 6, 7, and 8 with 5-fold cross-validation. Additionally, the 7th sensor alone demonstrated high performance with an accuracy of 90.51%. The use of FFT-transformed data further enhanced classification accuracy, with the highest being 92.06% for 3-fold cross-validation. The results suggest that the selected sensors, especially the 7th sensor, offer effective and economically viable solutions for tea classification.

articleTitle: Innovative Application of Tangible Interaction Narrative System in Visually Impaired Education from the Perspective of Informatics
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of poor self-learning ability of visually impaired learners, this paper uses the Tangible Interactive Narrative System (HCI). Conduct research on the accessibility of visually impaired learners. Firstly, according to the tangible and interactive effect of HCI on teaching content and the auxiliary characteristics, the evaluation of HCI human-computer interaction was established from the aspects of participation, comprehension, memory and retelling of visually impaired educational content, and the auxiliary effect of HCI human-computer interaction was defined through the judgment matrix. Then, the reliability of HCI human-computer interaction was analyzed by using the visually impaired education content, and the implementation plan of HCI human-computer interaction was designed, which effectively improved the stability of the transmission of visually impaired education and teaching content, and completed the practical test of HCI human-computer interaction. The simulation results show that HCI human-computer interaction has certain auxiliary value, which can effectively improve the memory of visually impaired learners and improve the accuracy of educational content delivery.

articleTitle: Secure Data Exchange Technologies in Mobile and IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: When transferring keys, passwords, authentication or personal data between mobile or IoT, there is a risk of information leakage. Standard radio transmission channels contain many vulnerabilities, difficulties in developing certification of the received tools. Optical means are sensitive to camera quality, screen condition, illumination, etc. The issues of acoustic information transmission are considered. The article is devoted to making a decision on choosing a suitable information transmission system depending on the transmission conditions and level of protection. Optical and acoustic transmission channels are chosen as the basic system.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Orange Quality Classification: A Hyperparameter Optimization Approach Through Puma Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Oranges are used in various industries, including food, beverage, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals, in addition to being consumed fresh. Traditional orange quality assessment methods are expensive and often lead to human errors. This study employs machine learning (ML) algorithms to significantly improve the accuracy of classifying orange quality. We conducted evaluations on multiple ML algorithms, specifically Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, Gradient Boosting (GB), and Decision Trees (DT). Among the evaluated methods, RF algorithm demonstrated the best performance, initially achieving an accuracy rate of 75.51%. To enhance model performance, we utilized the newly developed Puma Optimizer Algorithm (POA) for hyperparameter optimization. Following optimization, the accuracy of RF algorithm increased to 81.63%. Meanwhile, XGBoost and GB achieved an accuracy of 79.59%, and the DT model saw an improvement to 63.27%. The results were validated using a set of metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, along with correlation and confusion matrices. The enhancements in classification performance underscore the effectiveness of ML algorithms in practical agricultural applications.

articleTitle: Methodological Foundations for Constructing Intelligent Information Security Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence, the emergence of full-scale quantum computers form a new level of computing capabilities of intruders (cyberterrorists). At the same time, financial and energy costs for the implementation of targeted (mixed) attacks are significantly reduced, which, in combination with the development of smart technologies, provides evil to almost any critical infrastructure objects, on the one hand. On the other hand, the evolutionary development of the IT industry "ensures" an increase in the areas of human activity that must be included in the list of critical infrastructure objects. The paper proposes conceptual (methodological) foundations for building intelligent protection systems that can provide the required level of security in the post-quantum period.

articleTitle: Dam Water Levels Prediction Using Different Time Series Models for Yusufeli and Deriner Dams
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In this study, water level prediction was conducted for the strategically important Yusufeli and Deriner Dams, located on the Çoruh River in Turkey. With a height of 275 meters, Yusufeli Dam is the tallest dam in Turkey and plays a crucial role in energy production and flood control. Similarly, Deriner Dam, standing at 249 meters, is the second tallest dam in the country and significantly contributes to the region’s hydroelectric energy capacity. Accurate water level prediction is critical for ensuring the sustainability of hydroelectric power generation, effective flood management, and efficient water resource utilization. The study employed time series analysis techniques, utilizing ARIMA, SARIMA, ARIMAX, and SARIMAX models to forecast water levels, and their predictive performances were compared. The analysis for Deriner Dam demonstrated that the SARIMAX model achieved the highest accuracy with an R<sup>2</sup> score of 99.05%. Conversely, for Yusufeli Dam, the ARIMA model exhibited the best performance with an R<sup>2</sup> score of 99.32%. Furthermore, the study compared the predictive performance of the employed models with similar studies in the literature, revealing that the proposed models offer high accuracy. The findings indicate that time series models provide reliable and effective results in hydrological forecasting. For future research, it is recommended to test model performance in different hydrological systems and assess the long-term impacts of climate change on water level predictions.

articleTitle: A Digitalized Business Wargame Model for Foresight-based Future Planning and Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In an increasingly uncertain business world, futuristic thinking and foresight analysis methods are of great importance to support companies’ future-oriented decisions. Foresight analysis uses techniques such as scenario planning and trend monitoring to reduce future uncertainties. These analyses enable companies to make more informed decisions about future possibilities and play a crucial role in risk management.This article aims to develop a digital platform that simulates foresight-based decision-making processes based on business wargaming principles. Designed in a foresight-based card game format, the simulation allows players to model the competitive environment through various scenarios and evaluate long-term impacts. This game format helps users enhance their futures thinking skills and prepare for potential futures.The system is developed using C# and Unity, supported by pre-trained language models. Additionally, a PostgreSQL-based data management system is used to analyze user interactions and decision processes. This article describes an innovative solution developed in collaboration with TUSAŞ for sectoral decision-making mechanisms. The digital platform presented aims to help companies be more flexible and proactive in their foresight-based planning processes, thus enabling them to adapt more quickly to changing market conditions.

articleTitle: Optimized YOLOv8 (YOLO-Prime), M-CNN, and Dynamic Linear Regression for Real-Time Aerial Vehicle Detection in Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: This paper introduces a modified architecture of YOLOv8, called YOLO-Prime, to detect aerial vehicles. By employing YOLO-Prime to embedded systems such as Nvidia Jetson Xavier Nx and Rockchip 3588, we reduced the inference time by 130% compared to the YOLOv8m model and by 158% compared to the YOLOv8l model. In addition to YOLO-Prime, we present a Morphological CNN (M-CNN) to classify regions detected by YOLO-Prime. With the integration of M-CNN, we achieved an increase in detection accuracy by 20% in the detection of aerial vehicles. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic linear regression model to predict the future coordinates of aerial vehicles. As a result of the integration of dynamic linear regression models to embedded systems, GPU utilization of deep learning models decreased by approximately 66%. In summary, the combination of YOLO-Prime, M-CNN, and the dynamic linear regression model contributes to detecting aerial vehicles in embedded systems where energy consumption, inference time, and accuracy are crucial for realtime applications.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Impacts of NLP and Chatbot Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into digital transformation processes in Turkey plays a significant role in the dissemination of high-tech products. Large Language Models (LLMs) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques are supported by innovative solutions developed by HAVELSAN. During this process, Turkey's AI development capacity is increasing, and its competitiveness is being strengthened. HAVELSAN addresses public and private sector demands by developing national products, aiming for an 18.79% resource saving in enterprise content management and a 34.46% reduction in information access time through digital assistants. The solutions safeguard user data in compliance with international ISO 27001 and GDPR standards. The proliferation of high-tech products has increased the number of AI-based solutions by 48.27%, and patented solutions have boosted the success rate of technological projects by 40.12%. National AI products have expanded their domestic market share by 30%, revitalizing the local ecosystem while playing a significant role in entering international markets. These advancements strengthen Turkey's position as a regional leader in artificial intelligence and facilitate the achievement of its future technological goals.

articleTitle: Autonomous UAV-Based Monitoring of Fuel Tanks Using YOLOv8 for Global Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the detection of fuel tanks, critical components of global energy management and infrastructure security, from UAV-acquired images using the YOLOv8 algorithm. The synergy between UAVs and the YOLOv8 object detector is highlighted, demonstrating its capacity to automate detection and monitoring processes for industrial control applications. YOLOv8's advanced architecture, featuring a robust backbone and efficient neck design, enables accurate detection of objects across various sizes and conditions, even within complex scenes. As the latest iteration of the YOLO series, YOLOv8 surpasses its predecessors in accuracy and processing speed, incorporating advanced features that enhance its detection capabilities. The study evaluates YOLOv8's performance in detecting fuel tanks under diverse scenarios. Key results include a sensitivity rate of 0.888, indicating high precision in positive predictions, and a recall rate of 0.896, reflecting a low target miss rate. The mean average precision (mAP) of 0.891 and F1 score of 0.892 underscore the algorithm's balanced optimization of accuracy and sensitivity. Additionally, YOLOv8 achieves a rapid processing time of 41 ms per image, highlighting its suitability for real-time applications. These findings contribute significantly to the adoption of innovative technologies in energy and industrial control sectors, demonstrating YOLOv8's effectiveness and reliability for automated monitoring tasks.

articleTitle: Prioritization of indicators in the scheduling of examinations for full-time students in higher education
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Identified the main indicators affecting the scheduling of examinations in a higher education institution. The assessment of priorities related to the indicators and their weighting coefficients was conducted using rank correlation and subjective statistical methods, based on the opinions of regular students. Consistency of opinions was assessed using Kendall's coefficient and statistical significance was tested using θ<sup>2</sup> -criteria. The results will be used to create a web-based system for generating an optimal examination timetable for regular students at a higher education institution.

articleTitle: ICT Applications in Business Model Innovation Driven by Information and Knowledge Management
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: To effectively manage information and knowledge management driven by the development of business model innovation, so as to reduce the development of system application, the research and the application of knowledge management driven business model innovation, and create a aims to maximize the development of information and knowledge management driven business model innovation application operation development optimization model, but also design an improved ICT to solve the model. In this study, the practical cases were used to verify the operability of the model and compared with the transmission algorithm to clarify the effectiveness of the algorithm. Obviously, if the operation of some business model innovation driven by information and knowledge management can be reasonably managed, the overall development of business model innovation driven by information and knowledge management can be significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Investigation of Depth Perception Through Gaming
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In this study, we investigate how depth cues and immersive 3-dimensional (3D) video content characteristics can activate mirror neuron activities and improve depth perception experience while playing a very well-known game (i.e., Tower of Hanoi). For these investigations, subjective tests are carried out by employing an auto-stereoscopic display, with content developed in Unity to replicate realistic environments and facilitate dynamic interactions, exemplified by the Tower of Hanoi game. Subjects are exposed to atmospheric perspective depth cue and 3D video content characteristics, including different viewing angles (i.e., 0°, 45°, and 60°) of the objects placed in the game. The findings indicate that enabling the atmospheric perspective depth cue and different viewing angles considerably enhanced depth perception and task performance, resulting in smoother and more immersive user experiences. We believe that significant insights from this investigation will provide the advance of future robotics, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), 3D video processing, and game technologies that aim to leverage mirror neuron activation to improve cognitive and motor skills in intricate tasks.

articleTitle: Products Purchased by Those Who Viewed This Item
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: This paper presents two recommendation models for e-commerce platforms, enhancing product discovery by suggesting alternatives based on historical purchasing patterns associated with product views. The first model employs a statistical approach, while the second utilizes a neural network-based two-tower architecture. Both models adhere to the "Products Purchased by Those Who Viewed This Item" principle. Extensive online A/B testing revealed that the statistical approach significantly improved click-through rates (CTR) by 2.55% and conversion rates (CR) by 0.51% compared to conventional similarity-based recommendation methods. However, the two-tower model, despite offering broader coverage, resulted in a 1% decrease in CTR and a 0.21% decrease in CR compared to the statistical approach. These findings underscore the potential of sophisticated modeling techniques to apply user behavior data, significantly enhancing user engagement and profitability in e-commerce settings. Consequently, the two-tower model is implemented as a supplementary recommendation system to enrich the user experience alongside the statistical approach.

articleTitle: Examining the Impacts of Different Characteristics of Water on Coplanar Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Antennas are subjected to diverse environmental conditions during the transmission or reception of signals in the form of electromagnetic waves. While designed to function outdoors or in environments conducive to minimal signal attenuation, they may not always operate under such ideal circumstances. Factors such as rain induced water puddles impinging on the antenna's radiation pattern can lead to wave attenuation. Given that the conductivity enables the electric transfer of water is approximately 80 times more effective than that of air, it significantly reduces the velocity of electromagnetic waves. Consequently, such issues give rise to undesirable conditions in S_11, a critical parameter for antennas. This analysis encompasses the theoretical, simulation, and fabrication phases of a coplanar patch antenna. S_11 input reflection values were measured utilizing a Nano-VNA across various environments, including saltwater collected from the coastal area of a district (Black Sea) in Düzce, Türkiye; freshwater from the market designated for drinking purposes; mineral water; initially from a fountain source cited in literature as a remedy for kidney ailments by local inhabitants; and in an open-air setting. Signal attenuation values were compared at approximately 2.1 GHz frequency and its vicinity. Upon completion of the modelling, testing, and evaluation, it was observed water primarily contributed to signal attenuation, rendering the antenna non-functional.

articleTitle: Design of Electronic Chess Board Using Analogue Hall-effect Sensors for Piece Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of an innovative electronic chess board leveraging Hall-effect sensors for chess piece identification. Current electronic chess boards employ diverse technologies such as RFID, resistive switches, optical sensors, and computer vision, each with varying complexity and cost. The proposed solution utilizes Hall-effect sensors to detect changes in magnetic flux density caused by magnets embedded in chess pieces.The design features a modular 4x4 grid of sensors integrated on printed circuit boards, where each piece is differentiated by a unique magnet-spacer configuration. Experimental investigations validate the relationship between magnetic flux density and distance, modelled theoretically and tested with a field strength meter and the PCB system. Results confirm the accurate detection of piece positions and classes, despite minor interference from adjacent pieces. A Python-based system processes the sensor data, translating chess moves into live updates on the Li-Chess platform.The system has displayed good results in piece position identification accurately. Further improvement including as spacer configurations are to be done to implement piece classification. Future work aims to explore enhanced micro-controller integration, offering a streamlined and accessible alternative to existing technologies.

articleTitle: Design of an Open Source Piezoelectric Devices for Road Systems of Republic of Türkiye
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The rapid human population and technological developments constantly increase the demand for energy resources. A significant portion of our energy needs is satisfied by fossil fuels. However, fossil fuels are rapidly depleting, and their usage processes lead to serious problems such as environmental pollution and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. CO₂ emissions accelerate global warming by increasing the accumulation of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, causing the melting of glaciers, rising sea levels and disrupting the natural balance. This situation requires the development of well-designed sustainable energy sources. The main goal of our paper is to create a sustainable method for producing energy by converting the pressure exerted by vehicles on the road surface into electrical energy. For this purpose, piezoelectric panels were placed under the asphalt base during the asphalt pavement with a lightweight track feature on the far-right lane of the roads. The pressure applied as the vehicles pass enables these panels to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy. The energy generated can be stored in capacitors to meet various energy demands. We believe that the proposed model will reduce carbon emissions by decreasing fossil fuel usage and minimizing environmental damage, contributing to a clean and sustainable future.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv9 for Real-Time Traffic Sign Detection in Intelligent Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Rapid urbanization and population growth have intensified transportation challenges and traffic safety concerns, driving advancements in autonomous driving systems and intelligent transportation systems (ITS). Within this context, accurate and efficient traffic sign detection plays a crucial role in enhancing road safety and optimizing traffic flow. This study presents an improved algorithm based on the YOLOv9 model, tailored for traffic sign detection in ITS applications. The proposed algorithm is evaluated against the baseline YOLOv9 model using a carefully prepared dataset, focusing on key performance metrics. Results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv9 model achieves approximately 3% enhancement in precision, recall, mean average precision (mAP), and F1 score compared to the original model. Furthermore, with a detection time of 8.22 ms, the algorithm is highly suitable for real-time applications. These findings underscore the potential of the enhanced YOLOv9 model in addressing critical ITS challenges and advancing the state-of-the-art in traffic sign detection.

articleTitle: “Is It Future or Is It Past?”: From Self-contained Microtasks to AI-driven Collaborative Crowdsourcing
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Interest in artificial intelligence (AI)-driven crowd work has increased during the last few years as a line of inquiry that expands upon prior research on microtasking to represent a means of scaling up complex tasks through AI mediation. Despite the increasing attention to the macrotask phenomenon in crowdsourcing, there is a need to understand the processes, elements, and constraints underlying the infrastructural and behavioral aspects in such form of crowd work when involving collaboration. To this end, this paper provides a first attempt to characterize some of the research conducted in this direction to identify important paths for an agenda comprising key drivers, challenges, and prospects for integrating human-centered AI in collaborative crowdsourcing environments.

articleTitle: Advancing Medical Video Question Answering Through Large Language Models, Temporal Localization and Causal Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In this research, we take an innovative approach to the Video Corpus Visual Answer Localization (VCVAL) task using the MedVidQA dataset. We expand on it by incorporating causal inference for medical videos, a novel approach in this field. By leveraging the state-of-the-art GPT-4 and Gemini Pro 1.5 models, the system aims to localize temporal segments in videos and analyze cause-effect relationships from subtitles to enhance medical decision-making. This paper extends the work from the MedVidQA challenge by introducing causality extraction to enhance the interpretability of localized video content. Subtitles are segmented to identify causal units such as cause, effect, condition, action, and signal. Prompts guide GPT-4 and Gemini Pro 1.5 in detecting and quantifying causal structures while analyzing explicit and implicit relationships, including those spanning multiple subtitle fragments. Our results reveal that both GPT-4 and Gemini Pro 1.5 perform better when handling queries individually but face challenges in batch processing for both temporal localization and causality extraction. Despite these challenges, our innovative approach has the potential to significantly advance the field of Health Informatics.In this research, we address the Video Corpus Visual Answer Localization (VCVAL) task using the MedVidQA dataset and take it a step further by integrating causal inference for medical videos. By leveraging the state-of-the-art GPT-4 and Gemini Pro 1.5 model, our system is designed to localize temporal segments in videos and analyze cause-effect relationships from subtitles to enhance medical decision-making. Our preliminary results indicate that while both models perform well for some videos, they face challenges for most, resulting in varying performance levels. The successful integration of temporal localization with causal inference can provide significant improvement for the scalability and overall performance of medical video analysis. Our work demonstrates how AI systems can uncover valuable insights from medical videos, driving significant progress in medical AI applications and potentially making significant contributions to the field.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Flow Channels in Reverse Osmosis Systems: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In saltwater desalination processes, fouling of the membrane utilized in the reverse osmosis (RO) system is an important issue that directly affects system performance. Membrane performance depends on various factors such as fouling concentration, fouling rate, membrane lifespan, and quality of the treated water. Various studies are being carried out on feed spacer geometry to reduce membrane fouling. Feed spacer geometries with wavy or sinusoidal geometries reduce concentration polarization (CP) by increasing flow rate and offer the best balance between energy efficiency and mass transfer. In this study, the effects of novel randomly generated feed spacer geometries on membrane performance were investigated by using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. The simulations incorporated the Navier-Stokes, advection-diffusion, Langmuir adsorption-desorption, permeate flux equations, and Darcy’s law, comparing these novel designs with existing flat geometry from the literature. The results indicate that innovative random feed spacer geometry designs effectively enhance the membrane performance compared to conventional flat feed spacer geometries, improving water quality and energy efficiency while minimizing pressure loss. These findings provide valuable insights for optimizing the trade-off between energy consumption and mass transfer performance in RO systems.

articleTitle: Cognitive Approach to Cybersecurity: Causality Analysis and Situational Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The dynamic nature of physical environments by their very nature and the explosive growth of data volume call into question the ability of socio-cyber-physical systems to perform adequate management actions on controlled physical assets in many contexts. The current state of cybersecurity requires the use of cognitive methods due to the increasing complexity, dynamism, and adaptability of threats. To quantitatively assess system security levels, aggregate data, and calculate the impact of various factors on the resilience of a cyber system, an approach combining causality analysis and situational learning has been proposed. The convolution in this approach allows for an integrated security assessment, taking into account asset criticality, attack probability, and the effectiveness of countermeasure mechanisms. The practical benefit of this approach is reflected in a significant reduction in response time to attacks. The main achievement of this approach is the ability to implement proactive protection, which anticipates attacks before they occur rather than merely reacting to them post-factum.

articleTitle: A Comparison Study on the Selection of the Optimum Electrical Equivalent Circuit Model for Lithium-Ion Batteries and Parameter Accuracy Analysis by the Least Squares Method
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The most commonly used methods for state of charge (SoC) estimation in lithium-ion batteries are Coulomb counting and data-driven approaches. However, both methods require high computational complexity and are associated with significant hardware costs. In many studies, equivalent circuit-based approaches that can be implemented on low-cost, resource-constrained processors have been explored as a solution to this problem. For this purpose, the Thevenin equivalent circuit model (ECM) was taken as reference and different electrical models such as 1RC, 2RC, and 3RC have been analyzed. The reliability of analyses conducted using equivalent circuits is directly related to the accuracy of the equivalent circuit parameters. Additionally, the number of parallel RC networks in the equivalent circuit positively impacts the accuracy of the analysis results. However, increasing the number of RC networks also raises the computational demand of the analysis. Therefore, significant efforts have been devoted to estimating battery parameters and identifying the most optimal circuit configuration. In this study, a nonlinear least squares method (LSM) is employed to minimize computational complexity while maintaining optimal accuracy. Furthermore, the impact of the number of parallel RC networks on accuracy is comparatively investigated. The accuracy of the estimated parameters is evaluated through US06 and UDDS driving cycle tests. The 1RC, 2RC, and 3RC models are compared using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values. As a result of the study, parameter estimations were achieved with over 98% accuracy.

articleTitle: A New Class of Dai-Liao Method for Solving Iteration Problems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: One of the key elements of conjugate gradient algorithms is the conjugate gradient directions. In this work, we used the modified secant equation to construct a new conjugate gradient coefficient. The global convergence and fundamental descent qualities of the derived algorithm set it apart and guarantee reliable performance in a variety of settings. Numerous numerical experiments on unconstrained optimisation issues have shown that the new formulae perform noticeably better than the current approaches. The performance of the suggested conjugate gradient scheme is specifically better than that of the conventional Hestenes-Stiefel (HS) conjugate gradient approach. The computing efficiency of unconstrained optimisation problems is improved by this development.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Emotion Recognition and Adaptive Teaching Strategies in Cross-Cultural Language Teaching
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: At present, the artificial intelligence-assisted emotion recognition technology of cross-cultural language teaching has the problems of poor recognition effect and poor adaptability. Therefore, this paper conducts in-depth research on the emotion recognition technology of artificial intelligence to cross-cultural language teaching. The optimization method of auxiliary emotion recognition technology for cross-cultural language teaching based on artificial intelligence algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the information of intercultural language teaching scene is extracted through the artificial intelligence framework, and the way of artificial intelligence is the integration of artificial intelligence nodes. Then, artificial intelligence algorithm is used to optimize the assisted emotion recognition technology of cross-cultural language teaching, and complete the optimization of artificial intelligence assisted emotion recognition technology of cross-cultural language teaching. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the effect of artificial intelligence-assisted emotion recognition technology in cross-cultural language teaching, improve the educational environment of artificial intelligence-assisted emotion recognition in cross-cultural language teaching, and optimize the experience of artificial intelligence-assisted emotion recognition technology in cross-cultural language teaching.

articleTitle: Enhancing Occupational Safety through Deep Learning-Based Helmet Detection in Hazardous Workplaces
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Construction sites are among the most hazardous workplaces globally, where non-compliance with protective equipment standards contributes significantly to workplace accidents, including severe head injuries. Helmets, a crucial component of personal protective equipment (PPE), play a vital role in mitigating risks and preventing fatalities. However, manual monitoring of helmet compliance is often inefficient and prone to errors. Recent advancements in technology, particularly in the field of deep learning-based object detection, present promising solutions. This study focuses on the application of the YOLOv7 algorithm for real-time helmet detection. YOLOv7, a version of the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family, offers an optimal balance between speed and accuracy, making it well-suited for detecting small, moving objects such as helmets in dynamic construction environments. The model was trained on a diverse dataset that included various helmet types, colors, and environmental conditions, and was exposed to a wide range of lighting and weather scenarios. Performance metrics, including precision, recall, mAP, and F1 score, were used to assess the model, demonstrating its superior detection capabilities compared to its predecessor, YOLOv8. YOLOv7 achieved an effective balance between computational efficiency and detection accuracy, underscoring its potential to enhance occupational safety. The results also emphasize the critical importance of integrating automated systems to enforce safety regulations and minimize workplace hazards.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Artificial Intelligence Models for Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: The increasing amount of information and content on the Internet has made it more difficult for users to access items that may interest them. Recommender systems have emerged to determine items that may affect users by filtering information obtained from users' behaviors through certain filters and presenting them to the user. This study presents the performance of widely preferred recommendation system models such as artificial neural network, XGBoost, KNNRegressor, and LightGBM models in the related literature. The well-known datasets, namely MovieLens-100k and MovieLens-32M, are used to evaluate these models. According to the presented results, it was observed that the artificial neural network model was ahead of other models in terms of performance data.

articleTitle: Scalable Optimization for Drone and Mobile Robot Routing Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: This study addresses the Drone Vehicle Routing Problem (TRPD) in a scenario involving a single drone and mobile robots, aiming to identify the optimal solution. A machine learning-based genetic algorithm (GA) approach utilizing function approximation is proposed, preserving a two-stage structure to enhance computational efficiency. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through numerical experiments and compared to the simulated annealing (SA) method under identical assumptions. The results demonstrate that the machine learning-based GA outperforms SA in solving small- and medium-sized problems, providing superior solutions in less time. However, for large-scale problems, the method exhibits slower performance due to the computational overhead associated with machine learning operations. These findings underscore the potential of integrating machine learning into optimization techniques to effectively address TRPD scenarios.

articleTitle: An Approach with Effective Guided Filter and Lipschitz Constraint Based CLAHE for Improving X-Ray Image Details
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to improve X-Ray image details. The image with increased contrast, edge enhancement and gradient change stability with this approach is used as input image in CLAHE algorithm. The proposed approach shows that X-Ray image details are significantly improved by enhancing contrast and edge enhancement. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fine-Grained Image Retrieval with Advanced Embedding and Loss Functions
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: This paper explores the optimization of similarity retrieval systems through the fine-tuning of embeddings using advanced loss functions, focusing on the Stanford Cars dataset. By employing Triplet Loss with hard and semi-hard negative sampling, alongside the ArcFace loss, we significantly enhance retrieval accuracy, demonstrated by increased Retrieval R-Precision. Our methodology includes robust preprocessing and data augmentation, utilizing a ResNet-based architecture to extract high-level image features. An efficient retrieval pipeline is established through the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) algorithm, ensuring real-time performance. The results indicate substantial improvements in capturing fine-grained visual similarities, with potential applications across autonomous vehicles, retail, and beyond. Future work will involve extending the approach to diverse datasets, exploring advanced architectures, and optimizing for real-time efficiency.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Adding a New Template to Network Management System and Zabbix Application
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In today's world, where institutional business processes are transferred to electronic environments, the real-time monitoring and management of software and hardware assets in institutional information systems are of great importance for ensuring business continuity. Information system software and hardware are managed using network management software. Due to the presence of numerous different brands of network devices, software, IoT devices, mobile computing devices, and cloud computing devices, network management software cannot recognize every type of device. Therefore, there is a need for methods that can efficiently and quickly introduce new and different devices to network management software.Within the scope of this article, approaches to adding software and hardware to the open-source network management system Zabbix are analyzed. Templator tool was analyzed. The study examines how software and hardware can be quickly introduced by creating templates and provides an application of this process.

articleTitle: Design of Cloud Computing System for Optimized Power Electricity Consumption in Office Buildings
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: In an era of increasing energy demands and the need for sustainable practices, this project presents the design and implementation of a cloud-based system to optimize electricity consumption in office buildings. The system integrates an Arduino Uno microcontroller, leveraging an LDR sensor to monitor light intensity, an SHT21 sensor for temperature and humidity readings, and an air quality sensor to measure indoor environmental conditions. The 8-channel relay module controls electrical devices based on sensor readings and user-defined thresholds, ensuring optimal energy usage. Connectivity to the cloud is established using the ESP8266 Wi-Fi module, facilitating remote monitoring and control via the RemoteXY platform. This system enhances energy efficiency and provides real-time insights and automation capabilities, paving the way for smarter and greener office environments. The proposed system monitors the light intensity. Then it makes the decisions how many lamps will operate at that moment and do the same thing for the cooling and heating devices, also for air quality checks if there is any gas, make the fan work to reduce the effectiveness of the gas until the percentage of the gas be in the acceptable range; finally, the humidity has been checked by the SHT21 sensor. If the sensor's reading is over, the fan will operate until the humidity is normal.By this process, the electrical energy load will be reduced, and at the same time, the work environment will be enhanced. The proposed system uses the IOT principle to monitor the building anywhere. In addition to a monitor on the operating device, we can control the devices at the same time.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Telehealth: Enhancing Diagnostic, Monitoring, and Accessibility Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing telehealth by addressing persistent challenges in diagnosis, patient monitoring, and healthcare accessibility. This paper evaluates AI's integration into telehealth systems, emphasizing its transformative role in enhancing diagnostic precision, personalizing treatments, and bridging gaps in healthcare equity. The study explores methodologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics, presenting their impact on optimizing care delivery. Ethical implications and regulatory challenges are analyzed alongside future directions to establish AI as a cornerstone of digital healthcare innovation.

articleTitle: Dictionary-based data augmentation for Libyan dialect
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Data Augmentation (DA) is an important technique for limited resources languages to address the deficiency in data. It’s based on the generation of new instances to tackle imbalanced data. In this work, we implemented a data augmentation technique by using a dictionary to replace synonym or antonym words within the original text to generate new text. This must keep the semantic meaning of the text. In this paper, we present the Libyan Dialect Dictionary LDD which we have created in order to generate new comments/tweets from Arabic Sentiment Analysis dataset for Libyan Dialect in the Airline domain ASALDA. To evaluate the performance of sentiment classification of new augmented data, three deep learning (DL) models LSTM, CNN, and RNN were used. The result confirms that the LSTM model achieved the highest accuracy of 94% when using original data in the test set and augmented data in the train and dev set. The LDD proposed in this paper can be used for all researchers who work on Libyan dialects and data augmentation.

articleTitle: Analyzing Correlations Between Refined Comfort Score, Usability, and Performance in Assistive Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Assistive technology (AT) enhances accessibility and usability for persons with disabilities. Prior research identifies the disability paradox, where persons with disabilities rate assistive systems more favorably despite lower objective performance. However, the extent to which subjective comfort influences usability and task performance remains unclear. This study applies a standardized approach to quantifying comfort through the Refined Comfort Score (RCS), which aggregates thirteen items from the Device Assessment Questionnaire to assess overall user comfort. By analyzing RCS, perceived usability from the System Usability Scale, and objective performance indicators such as task completion and task duration, this study examines how comfort and usability interact across user groups. The findings reveal that higher RCS strongly correlates with greater usability perception in both groups, yet its influence on task performance differs. Among persons with disabilities, higher RCS significantly correlates with increased task completion, whereas this relationship is absent for persons without disabilities. Feature importance analysis further highlights that comfort is the dominant determinant of task completion for persons with disabilities, while usability plays a greater role for persons without disabilities. These results suggest that comfort is a key factor in AT effectiveness, particularly for persons with disabilities. This study emphasizes the need to integrate comfort metrics into AT design and evaluation within human-computer interaction, ensuring usability improvements align with diverse user needs.

articleTitle: Design of Assistive Wearable Smart Belt for Patients with Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: There are approximately 10 million people with Parkinson's disease (PD) worldwide, and these statistics show that this value will reach 18 million by 2040. Parkinson's is a neurodegenerative, progressive disease that can be in sight in older people but also the younger population. As the disease progresses, conditions such as posture disorders, falls, and dementia may also occur. One of the most challenging and restrictive conditions for Parkinson's patients in daily life is the "Freeze of Gait" (F.o.G). This study aims to propose and present a design process for an electronic smart belt to increase the mobility and life quality of patients with Parkinson's disease in the case of a freeze of gait. During the design step, Arduino Pro Micro, laser diode, gyroscope and IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) sensors were preferred, immediately detecting the user's F.o.G (Freeze of Gait) condition. The work process of the proposed smart belt begins by transmitting the gyroscope data to Arduino Pro Micro. The mainboard activates the laser diode and provides a visual stimulus by drawing a laser walking line in front of the patient. This system allows the patient's relatives to be instantly informed about the F.o.G situation, even if they are far from the person they care for, with the help of SMS-retrieved location data from a GSM sensor. Sensors and circuits are integrated into the belt prototype, which is designed based on the universal design principle and tested for the usability step. Laboratory assessments show that the proposed model is ready for use and serial production. We believe this study will improve the quality of life of patients with Parkinson's and reduce their dependence on extra carers such as nurses. Also, this model sheds new light on new projects for designing assistive technologies for individuals struggling with Parkinson's.

articleTitle: Prediction of fake news on X: An analysis of LLMs and machine learning methods on TruthSeeker
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Communication has developed with technology and become a global network. Social media platforms like X make it very easy to share information. This causes fake and misleading news to spread rapidly in society. Because in these new ways of obtaining information, some difficulties arise in determining the reliability and accuracy of information. In order to overcome these difficulties, machine learning and natural language processing techniques play an important role today. In this study, a highly reliable and effective approach has been presented using the TruthSeeker dataset, large language models (LLM) and machine learning (ML) techniques to detect fake news on the X platform. Comparative and different variation tests of 12 different ML models and 6 LLMs have been performed for the proposed model and it is aimed to detect whether the news is fake or not binary. As a result of the experiments, 92.8% accuracy value was obtained with BERTweet and the original Soft Voting Ensemble structure, while 92.9% F1-score value was achieved. The 10-Fold CV-AUC value was 0.976 on average and its standard deviation was 0.001. This proves that the data dependency of the proposed model is quite low. In addition, the obtained results showed that the model can detect fake news with higher success than real news. The obtained results show that BERTweet and Voting Soft Ensemble models can be effective and reliable tools in the task of fake news detection. In addition, with the proposed model, it will be possible to prevent the spread of misleading news and protect users, and the social impact of these news will be reduced.

articleTitle: Implementation of 3D U-NET for Lung Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Cancer is a significant health issue that is spreading quickly worldwide and is challenging to control. Various types of cancer negatively impact people’s quality of life and considerably raise mortality rates. Factors such as smoking, genetic predisposition, and air pollution significantly contribute to the development of lung cancer. Lung cancer is one of the most common types of cancer worldwide and can progress rapidly, posing a serious threat to life if left untreated. However, if the disease is diagnosed early, the chances of successful treatment significantly increase, leading to better patient survival rates. Early diagnosis of lung cancer is critically essential for extending patient life spans. Research into early diagnosis and detection are examples of effective assistive treatment that continue to develop nowadays. For this reason, early diagnosis of lung cancer is of critical importance in terms of extending the life span of patients. Nowadays, studies on early diagnosis and correct treatment continue unabated. In this project, a deep learning model based on the 3D U-Net architecture was developed to detect lung cancer. The model assists in the earlier and more accurate diagnosis of abnormalities in medical images using deep learning techniques. The study utilized the "Lung-PET-CT-Dx" algorithms on a large dataset of 232,389 DICOM images for lung cancer diagnosis. Various data preprocessing techniques were implemented during the implementation phase, leading to a proposed model that demonstrated 95.64% accuracy in diagnosing lung cancer and staging and detecting medical abnormalities. We believe that the developed model will shed light on new studies on applying deep learning for the early detection of lung cancer.

articleTitle: Implementation of Bavesian Theory in Fire Credit Evaluation: Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Fire credit assessment, belongs to is the sustainable development of fire credit assessment security theory, the theory to fire credit assessment, to a certain extent, can protect the fire credit assessment safety environment, reduce energy consumption, therefore, this paper to barvicon theory to the fire credit assessment and protection mechanism of in-depth analysis. Firstly, the gray correlation theory is used to analyze the characteristic indicators in the fire credit evaluation and protection mechanism to construct the estimation index system of the fire credit evaluation and protection mechanism. Then adopt Bavison theory to build fire credit assessment and protection mechanism control explanatory variables and control variables, through the principal component analysis of fire credit assessment and protection mechanism control variation factor, the elastic modulus and regression discrimination method, complete Bavison theory to the impact of fire credit assessment and protection mechanism. The simulation results show that the algorithm can reduce the economic cost of fire credit assessment, ensure the quality of the theory, and protect the safe environment of fire protection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Explainability of Chemical Oxygen Demand Prediction Models for Industrial Wastewater Treatment in Delfzijl, the Netherlands
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: Wastewater treatment is a vital solution that will reduce environmental effects by removing unwanted organic waste and producing a sustainable water source. However, the fundamental issue in running a wastewater treatment facilities is the excess chemical oxygen demand concentration due to sludge thickening. The quality of the WWTP’s effluent will decrease due to sludge thickening as a result of excess concentration of COD which will lead to decrease treatment efficiency, increased operational challenges, environmental harm to high aquatic life, and unpleasant odours. Consequently, one of the crucial problems that must be resolved to guarantee process safety and enhance effluent quality is the accurate identification of COD concentration. Machine learning, a branch of artificial intelligence (AI), is regarded as having the potential to disrupt global economies, environments, and communities by enabling systems to learn directly from data, examples, and experience without the need for pre-established rules. This research work made extensive analysis the estimated the concentration of COD level of Industrial Wastewater Treatment Plant which is located in Delfzijl City of the Netherlands, using sophisticated machine learning such as CatBoost model, XGBoost model and Random-Forest model for cost effectiveness and efficiency improvement of wastewater treatment facilities. The models demonstrated their capacity of handling the complexity in the dataset with prediction accuracy of 0.98.Additionally, to enable interpretation and highlight the features that contributed the most in the output of the models’ prediction, the SHAP explainer called SHapley Additive exPlanations was added and demonstrated a very good performance.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Beam Detection Data Optimization and Artificial Intelligence System Decision Support Based on MILP
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications (ICHORA)
abstract: At present, the artificial intelligence system decision support based on MILP beam detection data optimization, and the effect evaluation has a poor accuracy problem. Therefore, this paper studies the effect evaluation of artificial intelligence system decision support for beam detection data optimization. The evaluation model of decision support effect of artificial intelligence system for beam detection data optimization based on multiple beam detection data optimization is proposed. Firstly, principal component analysis is used to select the evaluation index of decision support effect of artificial intelligence system for beam detection data optimization.
